prior_year_events.impact_description: Impacted 2022 and contributed to elevated insured losses across the portfolio; cited as one of the major catastrophic drivers in 2022.
Gave rise to exposure that spreads across both the 2021 and 2022 Years of Account.

named_events.loss_description: Thought to be the second largest insured loss in history after Hurricane Katrina.

Based on the July 2023 Lloyd's RDS submission, industry loss estimate of US$131.0bn equates to a loss to the Syndicate of US$207.9m gross and US$85.3m net of reinsurance recoveries and reinstatement costs.

data.standardized_narrative: Opening gross claims outstanding at 1 January 2023 were GBP 380.805m. Analysis of the gross claims development triangle shows a net adverse prior-year development of approximately GBP 3.9m (about 1.02% of opening gross reserves), indicating a small strengthening of reserves overall. Management attributes reserve movements to prior large natural catastrophe activity (notably Hurricane Ian), geopolitical exposures (the Russian invasion of Ukraine) and related large-loss development, partially mitigated by reinsurance recoveries and portfolio remediation actions.
raw_causal_phrases: loss was dominated by heightened catastrophic activity and the conflict in Ukraine.

was impacted by Hurricane Ian, thought to be the second largest insured loss in history after Hurricane Katrina and a series of 'secondary perils' such as convective storms, straight line winds, winter freeze and widespread flooding and in addition the Russian invasion of Ukraine giving rise to exposure that spreads across both the 2021 and 2022 Years of Account.

Based on the July 2023 Lloyd's RDS submission, the largest Gross RDS was a Florida (MiamiDade) windstorm event with an industry loss estimate of US$131.0bn. This equates to a loss to the Syndicate of US$207.9m gross and US$85.3m net of reinsurance recoveries and reinstatement costs
data.data_quality_notes: Prior-year development (PYD) was not explicitly provided as a single gross figure. PYD was computed from the gross claims development (cumulative incurred) triangle by comparing current estimates to the previous diagonal for underwriting years up to 2021 (excluding 2022 and 2023) as described in the methodology. The technical provisions reconciliation table shows a total gross change in claims outstanding for the year of (39,186) (GBP '000) but this is the aggregate movement including current-year development; the specific PYD (older years) was derived from the triangle. LOB-specific reserve movements are not quantified in the report and are therefore left null. Amounts in the triangle and technical provisions are reported in GBP '000 (thousands) and have been converted to millions in the top-level monetary fields.
